subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing & discount ask
messages:
From: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit sizing — need finalize throughput/discount numbers

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We liked the consistent p95 you showed on the small proof-of-concept, but before procurement can move to a PO they need:

- a clear committed throughput (TPS) baseline we can rely on for seasonal spikes,
- an outline of the discount schedule for a 12 vs 24 month reserved commit, and
- evidence from a load test or benchmark that matches our expected request profile (40% chat-like prompts, 60% embeddings).

Can you share benchmark artifacts and a firm price band for 10k QPS-equivalent committed units? Procurement is targeting a decision by Apr 24.

Best,
Jenna
Jenna Ortiz
Director of Platform Partnerships | ACME Corp

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — need finalize throughput/discount numbers

Hi Jenna,

Thanks — we can definitely get you the artifacts. Quick summary and next steps:

- Committed sizing: based on the profile you described, our initial recommendation is a 24-card GPU pool sized to sustain 10k QPS-equivalent (mixed chat + embedding load) with a 95th percentile latency SLO of 150ms for generation-only requests and 60ms for embeddings.
- Discounts: we can offer a 12-month commit with 20% discount vs list, 24-month at 30% — final bands depend on exact throughput and burst guarantees.
- Benchmarks: Rishi will run a targeted load test that mirrors your 40/60 split and provide TPS, token-level cost, and p95/p99 latency traces. He will also include trace artifacts and a CSV of raw TPS numbers.

Can you confirm whether ACME requires cross-region failover (we should include that in sizing if so)? Assuming US-only initially.

I'll circulate the benchmark and a pricing PDF by EOD Apr 12.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — need finalize throughput/discount numbers

Hi all — benchmark results attached. Summary below:

- Test profile: 40% chat (avg prompt 180 tokens, gen length 120 tokens), 60% embeddings (256-dense vectors), mixed arrivals (Poisson) to simulate production variance.
- Sustained throughput: 10k QPS-equivalent sustained for 30 minutes with continuous batching enabled.
- P95 generation latency: 138ms
- P99 generation latency: 285ms (observed during two small spike windows correlated with cache-warm events)
- Embedding p95: 48ms
- CPU/GPU utilization: avg 78% GPU, 36% host CPU; headroom for 25% burst if autoscaling/burst capacity enabled.
- Cost projection: token-level unit cost estimate included in CSV (acme_dedicated_tps_report.csv).

Notes on traces: the attached latency_traces.zip contains raw traces; the two p99 spikes were due to KV cache eviction caused by overlapping long-context requests. Mitigation: pinning hot prefixes in cache or using a slightly larger KV cache reduces p99 to ~210ms in re-run.

Attachments: acme_dedicated_tps_report.csv, acme_latency_traces.zip

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML / Benchmarking | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acme.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — need finalize throughput/discount numbers

Thanks for the data, Rishi — helpful. A couple follow-ups from our infra and procurement teams:

1) The p99 spikes are concerning for our user experience. Can you confirm if the "pin hot prefixes" change is something we can ship/configure on day one of the Dedicated deployment? If it requires a code change we need roadmap timing.

2) On discounts: procurement asked for staged pricing bands tied to utilization. Example ask: 30% discount at 75% utilization guarantee, 35% at 90% utilization, plus a nominal $/min burst price. Is that something Redwood can support as a contractual clause?

3) Finally, for our legal team we'd like a short statement on auditability: can you commit to delivering token-level billing records and per-request traces for a rolling 90-day window?

Can your team put together a short 1-page note that addresses 1–3 so procurement can include it in the PO?

Regards,
Marcus Lee
Head of Platform Engineering | ACME Corp
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acme.com>, Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acme.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — need finalize throughput/discount numbers

Marcus / Jenna — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers below and an action list. I'll attach a one-pager and a draft contract clause to include in your PO.

1) P99 spikes and cache pinning: we can enable an "operational pin" for hot prefixes as a configuration knob at deployment time — no code change required. Rishi validated in a rerun that enabling the operational pin reduced observed p99 to ~210ms; if ACME needs aggressive p99 < 220ms we recommend: (a) the pin + modest KV cache increase (small config delta), or (b) add a 10% buffer to the pool sizing to reduce eviction likelihood. We will include both options in the one-pager.

2) Discount bands and utilization guarantees: we can offer staged pricing as a contractual schedule. Proposed structure: 24-month reserved commit at 32% baseline discount for the committed capacity, plus uplifted bands — additional 3% credit if monthly sustained utilization >= 90% (credit applied as invoice rebate), and 1.5% credit if >=75% sustained utilization. Burst pricing: $X/min (we'll specify exact $/min in the attached pricing PDF). This approach mirrors other enterprise deals and keeps billing transparent.

3) Auditability: Redwood will provide token-level billing and per-request trace metadata for a rolling 90-day window via our Console export APIs. We will include the export endpoints and sample payload format in the one-pager and covenant language for the SOW.

Action items:
- [Redwood] Attach one-pager + draft contract clause + finalized pricing PDF (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf) — due EOD Apr 21 (attached).
- [ACME] Confirm whether you want US-only or cross-region failover by Apr 23 so we can finalize sizing.

If that looks acceptable we'll prepare the PO template.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf
